title: Underlying quasi-coherence of a kernel from a free algebra-module sheaf
statement: Let S be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], A a quasi-coherent commutative O_S-algebra sheaf [def-weil-pbc-comm-algebra-sheaf, pqf-def-coherent], U any open, M an A|U-module on the slice site [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] whose underlying O_S|U-module is quasi-coherent, and g a morphism from the free A|U-module sheaf on any small type to M. Then the underlying O_S|U-module of ker g is quasi-coherent. U need not be affine and g need not be epi.

source.place: Schemes, Lemma 01IC and Section 01LA(5) (01LB); EGA I, Proposition 9.6.1

proof.text: Prove simultaneous preservation of small limits and colimits under scalar restriction. For each ring sheaf the forgetful functor simultaneously preserves limits and colimits by moduleSheaves_colimits_forgetful and reflects them by reflection of isomorphisms. Scalar restriction leaves its composite with the forgetful functor unchanged. Extract both preservation instances; kernels use the first and free coproducts use the second.

Compose scalar restriction with the equivalence from the slice to the open subscheme. Its image of the ring module is the restriction of the underlying algebra, hence quasi-coherent. Preservation of coproducts and closure of quasi-coherent modules under coproducts identify the underlying free term as quasi-coherent.

Prove that any module on the slice is quasi-coherent if and only if its image on the open subscheme is quasi-coherent. Use the Mathlib pushforward theorem for the equivalence of sites in each direction and the equivalence unit to recover the original slice module. Transport the quasi-coherent target forward by this equivalence, apply isQuasicoherent_kernel on the open subscheme, and use PreservesKernel.iso. Apply the reverse implication of the equivalence to obtain quasi-coherence of the scalar-restricted kernel.
